findings.source_passage: At the time, I devoted three days to the studious digesting of all this beer, beef, and bread, during which many profound thoughts were incidentally suggested to me, capable of a transcendental and Platonic application
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'At the time, I devoted three days'
findings.why_it_matters: This passage is a prime example of Ishmael's comic self-inflation and mock-scholarly voice — the claim to 'transcendental and Platonic application' from digesting beer lists is a signature ironic digression that establishes the narrator's satirical register.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'three days to the studious digesting' sentence with its 'transcendental and Platonic application' phrasing; the self-parody is core voice here.

findings.source_passage: Now, whether these gin and beer harpooneers, so fuddled as one might fancy them to have been, were the right sort of men to stand up in a boat's head, and take good aim at flying whales; this would seem somewhat improbable. Yet they did aim at them, and hit them too.
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'The quantity of beer, too, is very large'
findings.why_it_matters: This comic logical turn — admitting the improbability and then deflating it — is distinctively Ishmael's rhetorical style; its absence flattens the paragraph into dry summary and removes a characteristic voice beat.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the 'gin and beer harpooneers, so fuddled' passage with the concessive 'Yet they did aim at them, and hit them too' reversal.

findings.source_passage: But no more; enough has been said to show that the old Dutch whalers of two or three centuries ago were high livers; and that the English whalers have not neglected so excellent an example. For, say they, when cruising in an empty ship, if you can get nothing better out of the world, get a good dinner out of it, at least.
findings.why_it_matters: The draft conflates 'High livers, those Hollanders' with the closing maxim, losing the rhetorical pause and transition ('But no more; enough has been said') that frames the closing aphorism as a deliberate culmination.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'But no more; enough has been said' transitional framing before the closing maxim to preserve Melville's deliberate paragraph rhythm.

findings.source_passage: I was reinforced in this opinion by seeing that it was the production of one 'Fitz Swackhammer.'
findings.source_locator: paragraph beginning 'During my researches in the Leviathanic histories'
findings.why_it_matters: The mock-scholarly buildup — wrong conclusion from smell, wrong conclusion from title, wrong conclusion from author's name, then corrected by Dr. Snodhead — is a comic set-piece; the draft telescopes it and loses the layered irony of Ishmael's repeated misreadings.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the full sequence: smell → Cooper conclusion → Fitz Swackhammer reinforcement → Snodhead correction, to preserve the mock-scholarly comic rhythm.

summary: Three medium-severity failures (absent 'transcendental and Platonic' self-parody, absent 'fuddled harpooneers' comic reversal, flattened closing transition) together trigger regeneration; the draft strips the chapter's satirical mock-scholarly voice in its middle and closing paragraphs.
